subject: Carina — dedicated throughput corridor & GPU orchestration

Subject: Dedicated throughput corridor & recommended GPU orchestration

Alex / procurement team — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture a pragmatic sizing proposal (tokens/sec -> GPU mapping) plus an operational headroom plan we can include in the SOW. Attached is a simple ramp model with your expected traffic profile. High-level summary below and a couple of concrete next steps so procurement can progress.

Key assumptions
- Primary model for inference: Carina will run an L7-family 7B quantized variant (512 context typical).
- Production SLO: p95 latency <= 350ms for interactive requests (single-turn chat).
- Traffic pattern: baseline sustained ~15,000 tokens/sec during business hours; planned marketing spike up to ~45,000 tokens/sec for short bursts (10–30 minutes).

Initial recommendation (reserved + burst fabric)
- Reserved (Dedicated) commit: 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (sustained coverage for baseline with ~25% safety margin).
- Burst pool: additional 8 x A100-equivalent on a shared burst slab available for short-term scaling to cover the 45k t/s spikes.
- Fallback: Route overflow to Redwood Hosted fallback model variant (smaller quantized 7B) when burst pool saturated — slightly higher latency but preserves availability.

Sizing rationale (short)
- Based on latency/throughput profiling (see attachment), a single A100-equivalent delivers ~4.2k tokens/sec sustained for the selected model and batching regime (batch=64 / context=512) while keeping p95 ~= 280–320ms.
- Baseline need: 15k / 4.2k ≈ 3.6 -> round to 4 GPUs. Add 25% headroom -> 4 reserved.
- Peak need (45k): 45k / 4.2k ≈ 10.7 -> round up to 11; with reserved 4, add burst 8 to reach comfortable headroom and absorb scheduling inefficiencies.

Deliverables we can include in the SOW
- Dedicated capacity commit (4 reserved GPUs) with a defined burst policy (burst pool of 8 GPUs up to 90 minutes/day)
- Warm cache preloading window for scheduled marketing spikes (customer to provide 30-minute notice for large campaigns)
- Latency SLOs, alerts, and a documented fallback routing policy to hosted models

Next steps
1) If the sizing looks OK, can procurement sign the SOW draft? (I attached a 1-page proposal).
2) Marcus and Priyom — can you validate the per-GPU tokens/sec numbers vs the latest quantization kernels and update the spreadsheet? I attached the ramp model for clarity.

Thanks — kim

--
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Kim / Marcus — I reviewed the attachment and ran a short throughput sweep on the target L7-7B quantized variant. Notes below (keeping it pragmatic for SOW):

Profiling summary (batching tuned for latency)
- A100-80GB-equivalent (opt kernel set, int8-ish profile): ~4.2k tokens/sec sustained @ p95 280–320ms (batch=64, seq=512). Cold start penalty ~10–15% for first minute, then steady.
- A10g-equivalent (cost-efficient burst): ~1.6–1.9k tokens/sec sustained @ p95 ~420–520ms (batch=48) — good for non-interactive or tolerant requests.
- Quantized lower-memory 7B (int4 experimental): ~5.6k tokens/sec sustained but p95 variability; recommend using as an ops fallback and only after a short QA window.

Modeling math (conservative numbers used in attachment)
- Baseline 15,000 t/s -> use 3.6 A100 -> reserve 4 A100 (includes 10% infra inefficiency buffer)
- Peak 45,000 t/s -> 45,000 / 4.2k = 10.7 -> ceil = 11 A100 total. With 4 reserved, burst pool = 7. We recommend 8 to give extra headroom + time-slicing inefficiencies.
- If some burst traffic can be downgraded to A10g slab (cheaper but higher p95), we can offload ~8k t/s (approx 4 x A10g) which reduces A100 burst need to ~6–7 GPUs.

Operational recommendations
- Headroom: target 20–30% buffer on top of modeled peak for the first 90 days of production. After stable telemetry, we can right-size with a monthly cadence.
- Warm cache: require 30-minute campaign warm-up; otherwise expect a 10–20% increase in observed p95 during initial minutes.
- Canary & fallback: 10% of traffic routed to hosted fallback for the first week of each major release to catch regressions.

I updated the attached spreadsheet ("carina_ramp_model_v1.xlsx") with per-minute ramp sims and two slab scenarios: (A) aggressive/A100 heavy and (B) mixed-tier cheaper (A100 reserved + A10g burst).

If this looks good, I can produce a short ops-runbook snippet to include in the SOW (warm-up playbook, escalation points, throttling thresholds).

— Priyom
